note: The CLOSED set of figure kinds (kogaki#876, child of #875).
A kind is a SCHEMA OF ROLES AND NOTHING ELSE. It carries no words a
reader sees: `roles` names the positions a figure of this kind has, and
`relation` states in one line what holds between them. Neither is
rendered to a reader, and nothing here is subject matter.
A Move's optional `visual_form` block names one `kind` from this set and
maps EVERY role of that kind into the Move's own vocabulary - the terms
its `requires`/`effect`/`intent` already use. Ingestion validates exactly
three things (the closed kind set and the Move's visual_form): the kind
exists, every role of that kind is mapped, and no extra role is mapped.
It judges no wording.
`kind` is reserved and can never be a role name - the block is flat, so a
role named `kind` would be indistinguishable from the kind selector.
tools/move_ingest.py refuses this file if any kind declares one.
CLOSED means a new kind enters by editing this file under its own issue,
never by a Move naming one. A Move naming an unknown kind is refused by
name, which is what makes the set closed rather than advisory.
A form on a Move OBLIGES NO STEP TO USE IT. Nothing in the draft pipeline
reads this file to decide anything today; it is a vocabulary, not a gate.
SPEC REFERENCES IN THIS FILE (kogaki#902; one carrier, kogaki#982).
The rule these entries are written under - what a copy is, what the two
markers `[implemented-against: ...]` and `[see: ...]` mean, and why nothing
names a section number or a line range - lives in ONE place:
src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md. It is not restated here; fifteen copies of it had
already drifted into eight variants, which is what kogaki#982 collapsed.
